rationale_evidence.anchor: Epistemic type system != simple linear hierarchy; TypedDirectedGraph+TransformationRules+Invariants; formal computational-semantics tuple E=(T,R,I,P)
rationale_evidence.statement: States not all epistemic types form a simple ordered hierarchy (e.g. Prediction and Observation are not 'higher' or 'lower', just different semantic roles), giving EpistemicTypeSystem != SimpleLinearHierarchy; the better model is TypedDirectedGraph + TransformationRules + Invariants. Formalizes computational semantics as E = (T,R,I,P): T=epistemic types, R=permitted transformations, I=invariants, P=provenance rules, with type(x) in T for artifact x and a transformation r: T_i -> T_j valid only if its preconditions hold.

## Rationale

Formalizes computational semantics as E = (T,R,I,P): T=epistemic types, R=permitted transformations, I=invariants, P=provenance rules, with type(x) in T for artifact x and a transformation r: T_i -> T_j valid only if its preconditions hold. - [S0964] types=[FORMALIZATION, PRINCIPLE] scope=OBJECT — "Defines the candidate type set T = {Observation, Measurement, Evidence, Fact, Claim, Inference, Hypothesis, Prediction, CausalClaim, Counterfactual, Decision, Authorization, Action, Outcome} as semantic types, not merely database tables. States the type-safety principle: InvalidEpistemicTransformation ⇒ Rejected unless an explicit transformation exists (e.g. Measurement not-arrow VerifiedFact automatically; instead Measurement --Validation--> VerifiedFact). Draws the cast-vs-proof analogy: an unsafe cast like 'Measurement as Fact' must be avoided; KnowledgeOS instead requires Measurement --EvidenceValidation--> Evidence, a transformation producing a genuinely new epistemic object, with explicit preconditions (ValidUnit, ValidTimestamp, KnownSource, MeasurementQualityAcceptable)." (anchor: "Candidate epistemic type set T; type-safety principle; cast vs proof (no unsafe semantic casts)")
- [S0964] types=[EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Experiment 1: cast(Measurement,Fact) is Rejected -- PASS. Experiment 2: a properly validated measurement (calibrated instrument, valid unit/timestamp, acceptable uncertainty) run through Validate() correctly yields EvidenceCreated -- PASS. States Evidence !== Fact (Supports(E,p) does not mean p=True); models a typed relation Supports/Contradicts/Neutral(E,p) rather than embedding truth in the evidence object. Experiment 3: evidence supporting p at 0.7 attempted as p->Fact is Rejected absent an explicit domain rule -- PASS. Defines a typed Claim(p) with SupportSet/Uncertainty/Provenance/Validity metadata, and Hypothesis as a claim with its own lifecycle (EvidenceFor/EvidenceAgainst), not a Claim-plus-boolean. Experiment 4: Proposed->Investigating->Supported or Proposed->Refuted transitions are allowed, but no direct Proposed->VerifiedFact without required validation -- PASS. Defines Inference I=f(E_1,...,E_n,M) required to preserve DerivedFrom. Experiment 5: deleting an inference's dependency references yields InvalidProvenance/UntraceableInference rather than silently representing it as independently sourced -- PASS. Defines Prediction=Y-hat_{t+h}, Prediction not-arrow Outcome. Experiment 6: immediately recording a model's FailureTomorrow=True prediction as FailureOccurred=True is Rejected -- PASS; outcome instead requires Prediction --Observation--> OutcomeEvaluation for calibration. Requires a causal basis (experiment/CausalModel+Assumptions+Data) for CausalClaim(X,Y): Association not-arrow CausalClaim without justification. Experiment 7: Correlation(X,Y)=0.8 cast directly to CausalClaim is Rejected -- PASS. Requires Counterfactual to preserve Model/Assumptions/Uncertainty. Experiment 8: an estimated Y_i(0)=5.2 stored as Observed(Y_i(0)=5.2) is Rejected -- PASS. Requires Decision to be generated from Knowledge+Objective+Constraints+Policy: Knowledge not-arrow Decision without a decision context. Experiment 9: ChooseAction(K) with no objective/policy/alternatives is Underdetermined -- PASS. Requires Authorization ('the relevant authority permits a particular action under defined conditions'): Decision not-arrow Authorization automatically. Experiment 10: Decision(a1) forced to Authorization(a1) despite governance prohibiting a1 is Rejected -- PASS. States Authorization !== Action (authorized but execution may still fail). Experiment 11: an existing authorization with an unavailable execution service correctly yields Authorized=True, Executed=False -- PASS." (anchor: "Experiments 1-11: unsafe/validated promotion, evidence-to-fact, hypothesis lifecycle, provenance destruction, prediction/causal/counterfactual/decision/authorization/action type violations (all PASS)")
- [S0964] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=OBJECT — "Depicts the epistemic type graph Observation -> Measurement -> Evidence -> {Claim/Inference} -> {Hypothesis, Prediction, CausalClaim -> Counterfactual} -> Knowledge -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome, explicitly a typed semantic graph rather than a strict linear pipeline (evidence can support multiple claims, a claim can depend on multiple evidence items, a decision on multiple claims, one action can produce multiple outcomes) -- 'Directed Typed Provenance Graph'. Gives Hoare-style typed inference rules, e.g. Measurement(m),Valid(m) / Evidence(e); Evidence(e),InferenceRule(r) / Inference(i); Knowledge(k),DecisionPolicy(p),Feasible(A) / Decision(d) -- and explicitly prohibits the rule AIOutput(a) / VerifiedFact(f) since no valid epistemic rule establishes that transformation." (anchor: "Epistemic type graph (not a linear pipeline); typed inference rules; explicitly prohibited AIOutput->VerifiedFact rule")
- [S0964] types=[DISTINCTION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Distinguishes Syntactically possible (a database allows it) from Semantically admissible (the epistemic type system does not); defines TypeCheck(operation,input) -> Accept/Reject, e.g. TypeCheck(PromoteToFact,AIOutput)=Reject while TypeCheck(CreateHypothesis,AIOutput)=Accept. Experiment 12: AIOutput accepted for CreateHypothesis but rejected for CreateObservedFact -- PASS." (anchor: "Syntactically possible vs semantically admissible; type checker as Accept/Reject function (experiment 12)")
- [S0964] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Introduces refinement types beyond simple types: Measurement[Unit=degC], Probability[0<=p<=1] -- p=1.3 is invalid; for a distribution P(X=x_i)=p_i, requires p_i>=0 and sum_i p_i=1, 'machine-checkable invariants'. Experiment 13: P(A)=1.2 is Rejected -- PASS. Notes physical-quantity refinements (e.g. valid ranges for a measured quantity) can similarly be encoded as selected type-system invariants." (anchor: "Refinement types with machine-checkable mathematical invariants (probability bounds, distribution normalization)")
- [S0964] types=[WARNING, CORRECTION] scope=OBJECT — "Cautions against encoding every business rule into the epistemic type system -- that would recreate the God Object/God Model problem: TypeSystem != EntireBusinessDomain. States the type system should define SemanticBoundaries and InvariantRules, with bounded contexts (EvidenceContext owns Evidence, InferenceContext owns Inference, DecisionContext owns Decision) supplying domain-specific meaning, and a minimal shared kernel. Experiment 14: creating one universal KnowledgeObject with observation/evidence/model/decision/authorization/action fields all together yields the expected architectural result GodObjectRisk -- explicitly marked FAIL (the only non-PASS experiment in this file), corrected by using TypedArtifacts with explicit relationships instead of a UniversalKnowledgeObject." (anchor: "TypeSystem != EntireBusinessDomain; bounded-context type ownership; God-Object experiment (the step's one deliberate FAIL, corrected)")
- [S0964] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "States each typed transformation T1 --Transformation--> T2 (e.g. Observation --MeasurementExtraction--> Measurement --Validation--> Evidence --Inference--> Claim) should record Actor, Method, Version, Inputs, Output, Timestamp, ValidationStatus -- 'a computational provenance trail'. Experiment 15: transforming Evidence->Claim without recording the inference method yields IncompleteProvenance; the claim may still exist but its epistemic status should reflect the missing provenance -- PASS." (anchor: "Type conversion as an auditable event with transformation provenance; incomplete-provenance experiment")
- [S0964] types=[WARNING, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Warns TypeErasure (e.g. Prediction -> GenericText -> Fact) can cause epistemic corruption if downstream processes lose the original semantic type and incorrectly promote it. Experiment 16: converting a Prediction to plain text ('the system will fail tomorrow') and later processing that text as Fact is Rejected, or at minimum TypeUnknown -- PASS. Concludes fields like EpistemicType, Provenance, Validity, Source are not documentation but part of the semantic contract." (anchor: "Type erasure is dangerous; semantic-type-erasure experiment; metadata is part of the semantic contract")
- [S0964] types=[FORMALIZATION, PRINCIPLE, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Introduces I_TypePreservation: epistemic transformations must preserve or explicitly transform semantic type -- no silent type changes. Poses the monotonicity question: can knowledge always become 'stronger'? No -- new evidence can contradict an old claim, reducing confidence or invalidating it. Experiment 17: strong contradicting evidence moving P(p) from 0.9 to 0.2 is an allowed KnowledgeUpdate reduction -- PASS. Concludes K_{t+1} should be modeled as Update(K_t,E_new), not K_t union NewFacts, moving toward a NonMonotonicEpistemicSystem where new information may invalidate previous conclusions -- 'normal in real-world knowledge systems'. Experiment 18: invalidating E1 (with E1=>C1 previously established) sets ReviewRequired(C1) rather than leaving C1 silently valid -- PASS." (anchor: "Type preservation invariant I_TypePreservation; non-monotonic knowledge update (revision, not accumulation)")
- [S0964] types=[DISTINCTION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "States Type(C)=Claim does not change when its validity changes -- its status may become Disputed or Invalidated, giving Type != Status; a 'status' field must not be overloaded with semantic type -- EpistemicType and LifecycleStatus are separate dimensions. Experiment 19: a hypothesis becoming Supported keeps Type=Hypothesis unless an explicit promotion transformation changes its semantic role -- Type != Status -- PASS." (anchor: "Type != Status: EpistemicType and LifecycleStatus are separate dimensions")
- [S0964] types=[FORMALIZATION, ANALYSIS] scope=OBJECT — "States not all epistemic types form a simple ordered hierarchy (e.g. Prediction and Observation are not 'higher' or 'lower', just different semantic roles), giving EpistemicTypeSystem != SimpleLinearHierarchy; the better model is TypedDirectedGraph + TransformationRules + Invariants. Formalizes computational semantics as E = (T,R,I,P): T=epistemic types, R=permitted transformations, I=invariants, P=provenance rules, with type(x) in T for artifact x and a transformation r: T_i -> T_j valid only if its preconditions hold." (anchor: "Epistemic type system != simple linear hierarchy; TypedDirectedGraph+TransformationRules+Invariants; formal computational-semantics tuple E=(T,R,I,P)")
- [S0964] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Proposes a set of Epistemic Operations analogous to a formal language: observe(), measure(), validate(), infer(), hypothesize(), predict(), intervene(), decide(), authorize(), execute(), evaluate(), each with typed inputs/outputs, e.g. predict: Model x Evidence -> Prediction; evaluate: Prediction x Outcome -> Evaluation; authorize: Decision x Policy x Authority -> Authorization. Experiment 20: attempting authorize(Prediction) with no Decision present yields TypeError -- PASS. Draws the programming-language analogy: just as int+file is prevented, KnowledgeOS should prevent Prediction+Authorization when no valid semantic transformation exists -- EpistemicTypeError becomes a meaningful architectural concept, with example violations Prediction->Outcome without observation, Correlation->CausalClaim without justification, AIOutput->VerifiedFact without validation, Decision->Authorization without authority, Missing->Zero without explicit semantics, all instances of the same underlying Semantic type violation." (anchor: "Typed epistemic operations (observe/measure/validate/infer/hypothesize/predict/intervene/decide/authorize/execute/evaluate) with function signatures; invalid-operation type errors (experiment 20)")
- [S0964] types=[FORMALIZATION, RESTATEMENT] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "States the central architectural principle: KnowledgeOS should never silently strengthen the epistemic type of an artifact; a strengthening transformation must be Explicit + Validated + Provenanced + Governed. Consolidates six invariants: I_1 Type preservation (type changes require explicit transformation); I_2 Provenance (transformation outputs retain ancestry); I_3 No silent promotion (AI output cannot silently become fact); I_4 No causal promotion (association cannot silently become causation); I_5 No prediction promotion (prediction cannot silently become outcome); I_6 No decision promotion (decision cannot silently become authorization)." (anchor: "Central theorem: KnowledgeOS should never silently strengthen an artifact's epistemic type; six named invariants I_1-I_6")
- [S0964] types=[RESTATEMENT, OPEN-QUESTION, FUTURE-RESEARCH] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Declares STEP 67 -- PASS, 'a significant milestone': the move from epistemic concepts to epistemic computational semantics. Redescribes KnowledgeOS as 'a governed, provenance-aware, typed computational system for transforming observations into knowledge, decisions, and controlled actions' -- the word 'typed' emphasized as meaning the system can reject semantically invalid transformations before they enter the trusted knowledge state. Gives the current overall architecture diagram (Reality->Observation->Measurement->Evidence->Inference->Knowledge, branching to Prediction and CausalAnalysis, and to Decision via +Policy+Objective, then Authorization via +Authority, then Action->Outcome->Evaluation->Learning). Opens Step 68 (Contradiction, Paraconsistency and Knowledge Revision): whether KnowledgeOS can safely represent p and not-p without collapsing (avoiding the classical p ∧ not-p ⇒ everything-is-true disaster), given that conflicting-but-legitimate evidence can arise from different observation times, populations, contexts, measurements, competing models, genuine uncertainty, conflicting authorities, or an actual world inconsistency -- testing paraconsistent reasoning and belief revision as 'a useful knowledge system must remain operational in the presence of contradiction'." (anchor: "Step 67 verdict; KnowledgeOS redescribed as a governed, provenance-aware, typed computational system; opens Step 68 on contradiction/paraconsistency")
- [S0967] types=[EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Experiment 1: computing T(S0,e1) yields S1 as ordinary computation -- PASS. Experiment 2: attempting Prediction->VerifiedFact with no validation evidence yields T(S,e)=EpistemicTypeError -- PASS, illustrating that deterministic rule evaluation (if type(x)=Prediction and target=VerifiedFact and not-Validated then Reject) does not require an AI to 'understand' the rule -- 'exactly where deterministic assurance becomes powerful'. Separates deterministic computation f(x)=y from probabilistic computation P(Y|X): the deterministic layer verifies schema/type/provenance/authorization/invariant-satisfaction/graph-integrity/version-compatibility/cryptographic-integrity, while the AI/statistical layer performs inference/prediction/classification/hypothesis-generation/probabilistic-reasoning -- giving 'AI reasoning + Deterministic assurance'. Experiment 3: an AI output P(p)=0.82 checked deterministically for 0<=0.82<=1 plus ModelVersion/Provenance yields AcceptedAsProbabilisticClaim -- PASS." (anchor: "Experiments 1-3: finite state transition, invalid-type-transition rejection, deterministic-bounds-checked probabilistic claim acceptance")
